answer: In an agent market for crystal samples, dune surveys, and knoll maps, each seller locks tokens for 30 days, and its share of incoming jobs is proportional to that stake. Splitting 100 tokens among a thousand fake identities earns the same total allocation as staking them under one name. To capture more work, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens, tying up capital for the full period instead of gaining influence by creating accounts.
